A.explanation: Too small for the sleeve showing past $2.0\text{ mm}$ plus the $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark in diagram 1. It misreads the main scale.

B.explanation: Corrects the $2.59\text{ mm}$ observed reading in diagram 1 by subtracting the $+0.14\text{ mm}$ zero error in diagram 2 to give $2.45\text{ mm}$.

C.explanation: This is the uncorrected diagram 1 reading of $2.50\text{ mm} + 0.09\text{ mm} = 2.59\text{ mm}$. It ignores the positive zero error.

D.explanation: This adds the $0.14\text{ mm}$ zero error instead of subtracting it, giving $2.59\text{ mm} + 0.14\text{ mm} = 2.73\text{ mm}$.

hints: Look at the horizontal sleeve in diagram 1: count how many whole $1.0\text{ mm}$ marks and whether the $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark past $2.0\text{ mm}$ is visible, then add the thimble reading near $9$.
Recall that each thimble division is $0.01\text{ mm}$, so a thimble line at $9$ means $0.09\text{ mm}$ and a line at $14$ means $0.14\text{ mm}$.
Diagram 2 with closed jaws should read zero: a reading above zero is a positive zero error that must be subtracted from the diagram 1 reading to get the true diameter.
walkthrough: Read diagram 1 with the wire. The sleeve shows $2.0\text{ mm}$ plus the $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark is exposed, so main scale $= 2.50\text{ mm}$. The thimble datum aligns near $9$, so thimble $= 9 \times 0.01\text{ mm} = 0.09\text{ mm}$.

Read diagram 2 with jaws closed to find zero error. The sleeve shows no $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark, so main scale $= 0.00\text{ mm}$. The thimble reads $14$, so zero reading $= 14 \times 0.01\text{ mm} = 0.14\text{ mm}$.
Because the closed micrometer reads $+0.14\text{ mm}$ instead of zero, this is a positive zero error. True value $=$ observed $-$ zero error.
True diameter $= 2.59\text{ mm} - 0.14\text{ mm} = 2.45\text{ mm}$. This is option B.
